title: Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading that extends Minimum Energy Performance Standards and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use, and empowers the Minister to make regulations for online platforms to remove non-compliant listings.
why_it_matters: From 1 July 2026, end users importing regulated goods for their own use are to register with NEA, meet MEPS and carry MELS labels, with fines up to $10,000 per import for non-compliance. Registration and renewal fees for end users are to be waived, and existing schemes such as the Energy Efficiency Grant and Climate Vouchers are cited as support. The Bill excludes second-hand or used regulated goods and regulated lamps.

key_points.point: The Senior Minister of State moved that the Bill be now read a Second time.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: That the Bill be now read a Second time.

key_points.point: The Bill seeks to introduce MEPS and MELS to regulated goods imported by end users for their own use.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the Energy Conservation (Amendment) Bill seeks to introduce Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) and the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme (MELS) to Regulated Goods that are imported by end users for their own use.

key_points.point: End users would have to register regulated goods brought in for own use, meet MEPS and label them under MELS.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: End users would be required to ensure that regulated goods brought into Singapore for own use are registered with NEA, meet MEPS in accordance with prescribed international test standards and test conditions, and are labelled with the required energy labels under MELS.

key_points.point: The proposed regulations exclude second-hand or used regulated goods.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The proposed regulations exclude second-hand or used regulated goods where it is impractical to assess MEPS compliance.

key_points.point: Registration fees are to be waived for end users importing for their own use.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: this will be waived for end users who typically cannot spread registration costs across multiple units.

key_points.point: End users can rely on test reports from overseas suppliers and manufacturers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: end users can rely on test reports from overseas suppliers and manufacturers.

key_points.point: The compliance requirements extend to all regulated goods imported for own use, except regulated lamps.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The compliance requirements will extend to all regulated goods imported for own use, except regulated lamps.

key_points.point: The enforcement regime is intended to take effect from 1 July 2026.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: We intend to effect the enforcement regime from 1 July 2026 to deter end users from importing non-compliant regulated goods for own use and ensure compliance to the new requirements.

key_points.point: End users importing non-compliant regulated goods for own use face fines of up to $10,000 per import.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: End users who import regulated goods that do not comply with MEPS and MELS requirements will face penalties of up to $10,000 in fines per import.

key_points.point: The Bill empowers the Minister to make regulations to compel online platforms to remove non-compliant listings.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The proposed amendments to the Energy Conservation Act will also empower the Minister to make regulations to compel online platforms in Singapore or with a business establishment in Singapore to remove non-compliant listings.

key_points.point: The Energy Efficiency Grant covers up to 70% of costs for pre-approved energy efficient regulated goods.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: This Grant covers up to 70% of costs for pre-approved energy efficient regulated goods, such as three-tick refrigerators and five-tick air-conditioning units to help businesses improve energy efficiency outcomes.

key_points.point: Eligible HDB and private residential households can use $400 of Climate Vouchers for eligible energy efficient regulated goods.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Singaporean and Permanent Resident Housing and Development Board (HDB) Households as well as Singapore Citizen households living in private residential properties can use $400 of Climate Vouchers under the enhanced Climate Friendly Households Programme to purchase eligible energy efficient regulated goods.

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San said the amendment places the onus on end users to register imported regulated goods and demonstrate compliance.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
key_points.quote: It will place the onus on end users, to register the imported regulated goods with NEA and demonstrate evidence of compliance with the MEPS and MELS.

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San asked whether NEA has an estimate of appliances procured annually and total annual energy consumption.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
key_points.quote: does NEA have an estimate of the total number of electrical appliances and equipment that may be procured annually, as well as the total annual energy consumption?

key_points.point: Ms Poh Li San asked how NEA intends to police and enforce the new requirement given the large number of end users.
key_points.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
key_points.quote: given the large number of end users, how does NEA intend to police and enforce this new requirement?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong said the Workers' Party supports the intents of the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: the Workers' Party supports the intents of this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether there will be a grace period or simplified verification pathway for local micro-enterprises.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: Will there be a grace period or a simplified verification pathway for local micro-enterprises to ensure they are not crowded out of the digital marketplace by larger players with deeper pockets for compliance?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether a resident who later sells an imported non-compliant appliance becomes an unregistered supplier subject to prosecution.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: if a resident imports a non-compliant appliance for own use, but later decides to sell it because they have a change of mind, will they suddenly become an unregistered supplier subject to prosecution?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked whether the definition of regulated goods extends to firmware and software controlling energy consumption.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: does the definition of regulated goods under the act extend to the firmware and software that control energy consumption?

key_points.point: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong asked for the data-driven justification for excluding lighting from own-use import regulations at this stage.
key_points.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
key_points.quote: What is the specific data driven justification for excluding lighting from own-use import regulations at this stage?

key_points.point: Mr Ng Shi Xuan said SMEs may not realise they are legally treated as the importer even when they did not control the purchase.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
key_points.quote: end-users, such as SMEs, often operate through layered procurement arrangements and may not realise they are legally treated as the importer, even when they did not control the purchase.

key_points.point: Mr Ng Shi Xuan asked the Ministry to consider a transition period with fee support or waivers for SMEs, consumers and first-time applicants.
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Ministry to consider a transition period with fee support or waivers, especially for SMEs, consumers and first-time applicants.

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked whether the Ministry will work with Singapore Customs and Singapore Post on screening protocols for goods arriving by post or courier.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
key_points.quote: for goods arriving by post or courier, will the Ministry be working with Singapore Customs and Singapore Post to establish screening protocols.

key_points.point: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik asked for a clear interagency coordination framework between MSE and MOT and between NEA and other enforcement agencies.
key_points.speaker: Mr Abdul Muhaimin Abdul Malik
key_points.quote: there is a clear interagency coordination framework between MSE and MOT, as well as between NEA and other enforcement agencies with defined roles and responsibilities for each agency involved.

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe said the ordinary layperson does not think of himself or herself as an importer when buying goods from overseas.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: the ordinary layperson does not think of himself or herself as an importer when they purchase goods from overseas to Singapore.

key_points.point: Mr David Hoe asked how the Ministry intends to communicate the requirements to the public.
key_points.speaker: Mr David Hoe
key_points.quote: I would like to ask how the Ministry intends to communicate these requirements to the public.

key_points.point: Ms Valerie Lee asked whether there will be more targeted support, transitional assistance or differentiated timelines for smaller firms.
key_points.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
key_points.quote: Can the Ministry elaborate on whether there will be more targeted support, transitional assistance, or differentiated timelines beyond the current scheme for smaller firms?

key_points.point: Ms Valerie Lee asked whether the Ministry has sized the cost pass-through impact on consumers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Valerie Lee
key_points.quote: Has the Ministry sized this impact?

key_points.point: Mr Lee Hong Chuang suggested strengthening spot checks and independent assessment mechanisms.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
key_points.quote: I suggest the Government consider strengthening spot checks and independent assessment mechanisms to ensure energy efficiency standards can be implemented in real operations.

key_points.point: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui asked whether NEA has sufficient enforcement capacity and how it will prioritise the expanded responsibilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
key_points.quote: could the Minister clarify whether NEA has sufficient enforcement capacity, and how it intends to prioritise and operationalise these expanded responsibilities?

key_points.point: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui asked whether the Ministry would consider a shared product registry for product-level registration.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
key_points.quote: Would the Ministry consider a shared product registry that allows for product-level registration, while still maintaining accountability at the importer level?

key_points.point: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui asked how the Government intends to mitigate a potential surge in imports of non-compliant equipment ahead of the enforcement date.
key_points.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui
key_points.quote: Could the Senior Minister of State share how the Government intends to mitigate any potential surge in imports of non-compliant equipment ahead of the enforcement date?

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked whether simplified or streamlined processes will be available for SMEs and small-volume importers.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
key_points.quote: whether simplified or streamlined processes will be made available for SMEs as well as for individuals or businesses importing goods in small volumes.

key_points.point: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim urged the Government to consider placing clear obligations on platform operators to prevent non-compliant listings.
key_points.speaker: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim
key_points.quote: I urge the Government to consider placing clear obligations on platform operators to prevent the listing of non-compliant products in the first place.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether enough is being done to help households and businesses bridge higher upfront costs and lower long-term savings.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Are we doing enough to help households and businesses bridge the gap between higher upfront costs and lower long-term savings?

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether consumers will have a simple and accessible way to verify product compliance before purchase.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Will consumers have a simple and accessible way to verify whether a product is compliant before making a purchase?

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng said three months may not be sufficient for households, SMEs or businesses with goods already in transit.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Three months may not be sufficient for households amid renovation, SMEs amid procurement, or businesses with goods already in transit.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether the Ministry will provide regular reporting to Parliament on waivers, appeals and enforcement trends.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Will the Ministry provide regular reporting to Parliament on waivers granted, appeals outcomes and enforcement trends?

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang asked why an importer must register a regulated good even if another importer has already registered it.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify why this is required?

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang said it could be challenging for own-use importers to provide free-of-charge samples for testing and analysis.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: it could perhaps, be challenging for them to provide “free of charge” samples to the Director-General for the purpose of testing and analysis.

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang said the registration portal may need to be adapted to allow Singpass use by individual importers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: It may also need to be adapted to allow for the use of Singpass by individual importers.

key_points.point: Mr Foo Cexiang urged the agency to consider waiving or tiering registration charges for individual importers.
key_points.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang
key_points.quote: I urge the agency to consider whether these charges for individual importers can be waived or whether there can be a tiered registration system.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said only certain common appliances such as air-conditioners and refrigerators are covered under the Act and the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: only certain common appliances, such as air-conditioners and refrigerators are covered under the Energy Conservation Act and this Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said lights were excluded because regulating them would impose a disproportionate compliance burden on end users.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: we have excluded lights from the Bill because regulating them will impose a disproportionate compliance burden on end users, such as households that occasionally import a few lights.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said registration and renewal fees for end users importing regulated goods for own use will be waived.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the registration and renewal fees on end users who import regulated goods for their own use will be waived.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said all end users importing regulated goods for own use must register them with NEA regardless of prior registration by another importer or manufacturer.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: all end users importing the regulated goods for own use will be required to register them with NEA to demonstrate the MEPS and MELS compliance, regardless of whether another importer or manufacturer has registered such goods.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said NEA can accept test reports provided by equipment manufacturers for registration.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: NEA can accept test reports provided by equipment manufacturers for registration of regulated goods.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said end users are encouraged to register their regulated good prior to import.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: end users are also encouraged to register their regulated good prior to import to ensure that the good is MEPS- and MELS-compliant.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said NEA will upgrade the ELS Portal for a better user experience.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: NEA will upgrade the ELS Portal for a better user experience for those applying to register their appliance.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said testing analysis is conducted only on a needs-basis and where feasible.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: testing analysis is only conducted on regulated goods on a needs-basis and only where it is feasible to do so.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the Government would invoke powers to impose, modify or revoke conditions only on a needs-basis and with a reasonable time period for review, rectification and appeals.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the Government would only invoke these powers only on a needs-basis and a reasonable time period will be accorded for the review, allow for rectifications and to process the appeals.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said MEPS and MELS requirements are applied at the point of import only for own use, similar to current local supply regulations.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: we have adopted a practical approach to apply MEPS and MELS requirements at the point of import only for own use, similar to the current regulations that apply requirements at the point of local supply.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said an intermediary importing regulated goods for subsequent supply to an SME would be responsible for compliance.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: it is the intermediary importing the regulated goods for subsequent supply to the SME that would be responsible for compliance.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said NEA will issue press releases and circulars to inform end users and businesses about the new regulations.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: NEA will issue press releases and circulars to inform end users and businesses about the new regulations

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the Government has assessed that there is no need to introduce controls at the point of import at this time.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: We have assessed that there is no need to introduce controls at the point of import at this time.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the actual removal of non-compliant listings will be done by the platform.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The actual operationalisation of removal of these listings will be done by the platform.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the new regulations will only apply to new regulated goods imported for own use.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The new regulations will only apply to new regulated goods imported into Singapore, for the purposes of own use.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the new regulations exclude second-hand or used regulated goods online or in the physical marketspace.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The new regulations also exclude second-hand or used regulated goods, whether it is online or in the physical marketspace.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said second-hand regulated goods imported for resale as brand-new will be subject to MEPS and MELS requirements.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: second-hand regulated goods imported into Singapore for resale as brand-new will be subject to the MEPS and MELS requirements.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the new regulations are intended to take effect from 1 July 2026 to give platform operators time to adjust.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: We intend to effect the new regulations from 1 July 2026 to give platform operators time to adjust to the new regulations.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said penalties will be imposed per import, with fines of up to $10,000 per import of non-compliant goods for own use.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Penalties will be imposed on a per-import basis, with fines of up to $10,000 per import of non-compliant goods for own use.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the Energy Efficiency Grant base tier has been expanded to all sectors and extended to 31 March 2028.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: the Energy Efficiency Grant base tier has been expanded to all sectors and support will be extended for another year, to 31 March 2028.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said households that have yet to use their $400 Climate Vouchers can do so up to 31 December 2027.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Households that have yet to use their $400 Climate Vouchers can do so up to 31 December 2027.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said from 15 April 2026 households can tap Climate Vouchers for a wider range of resource-efficient products.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: From 15 April 2026, households can tap on Climate Vouchers to access a wider range of resource-efficient products and achieve greater resource efficiency.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said NEA, the Singapore Institute of Technology and the Energy Efficiency Training Centre launched the new Energy Efficiency Training Facility in February 2026.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: in February 2026, NEA, the Singapore Institute of Technology and the Energy Efficiency Training Centre launched the new Energy Efficiency Training Facility.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said NEA maintains an online database of compliant regulated goods with product information including estimated annual energy consumption and energy costs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: NEA maintains an online database of compliant regulated goods with product information, including estimated annual energy consumption and energy costs.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the Government does not yet know the number of goods because the extension is to goods currently not regulated.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: we do not yet know because the extension of the Energy Conservation Act is to goods that are currently not regulated.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said most businesses involved are already engaged with MEPS- and MELS-compliant suppliers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: most of the businesses involved are already engaged with MEPS- and MELS-compliant suppliers and are already involved with purchasing from the suppliers.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said software-driven degradation is a hypothetical situation not yet encountered.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: this is a hypothetical situation that we have not encountered yet.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said the Act provides for the Director-General and NEA to exercise a range of measures if a good is non-compliant or subsequently becomes non-compliant.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: The Act provides for the Director-General and NEA to exercise a range of measures should they come across a good, which is non-compliant or which was declared to be compliant and is now subsequently non-compliant.

key_points.point: Dr Janil Puthucheary said enforcement action could potentially be taken against both the importer and the manufacturer.
key_points.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
key_points.quote: Whether the action would be taken against the person who imported or the manufacturer, the answer is potentially both

what_happens_next: The Senior Minister of State said the new regulations are intended to take effect from 1 July 2026; the transcript does not record a vote or later stage.
not_said: How many regulated goods are currently imported for own use, and what is their total annual energy consumption?
What is the projected reduction in energy consumption if all F&B businesses deploy MEPS- and MELS-compliant appliances?
How will NEA enforce the requirement for goods arriving by post, courier, land checkpoints, or checked baggage?
Will there be a transition period or fee support for SMEs, consumers and first-time applicants?
How will the Bill treat individuals who later sell an imported appliance on peer-to-peer platforms?
Will software-driven energy degradation after registration be regulated, and how?
Will lighting be included in the own-use import regime, and on what timeline?
Will waivers and Director-General decisions be published or reported in aggregated form?
Will online platforms be required to screen listings before they appear, and what consumer protections apply after payment?
Will the Energy Efficiency Grant be expanded to cover all regulated goods?
Will there be top-ups to the Climate Friendly Households Programme for lower-income families?
Will there be a shared product registry or simplified pathway for subsequent importers?
Will there be an interagency coordination framework and a single point of contact for importers?
Will there be public reporting to Parliament on waivers, appeals and enforcement trends?
Will there be a priority processing lane for SMEs with high-efficiency products?
What is the projected cost impact on households and SMEs?
Will compliant models remain competitively priced?
How will NEA distinguish deliberate circumvention from genuine misunderstanding?
Will registration of goods be retrospectively revoked if a software update degrades performance?
